name: Ribbon
rootCause: Ribbon Finance said in a tweet that the homepage of the URL suffered a DNS attack, causing 2 users to approve a malicious contract for vault deposits. At present, the team has solved the problem, and the funds in all contracts are in a safe state. After analyzing the data on the chain, SlowMist believes that it is the same attacker as Convex. At the same time, it is found that a user of Ribbon Finance lost 16.5 WBTC in the attack.

descriptions.text: Ribbon Finance said in a tweet that the homepage of the URL suffered a DNS attack, causing 2 users to approve a malicious contract for vault deposits. At present, the team has solved the problem, and the funds in all contracts are in a safe state. After analyzing the data on the chain, SlowMist believes that it is the same attacker as Convex. At the same time, it is found that a user of Ribbon Finance lost 16.5 WBTC in the attack.

On June 24, 2022, Ribbon Finance’s frontend was compromised by a DNS hijack at Namecheap, redirecting users to a phishing site. At least 16.5 wBTC was confirmed stolen by the attacker, with additional claims of rETH and stETH losses based on forum estimates. No protocol contract was exploited. A compromised customer support agent account at Namecheap enabled an attacker to alter ribbon.finance's DNS records, diverting users to a phishing site and capturing approvals and deposits. No vulnerability existed in Ribbon's smart contracts.
